chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Baseer and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The wheat and the barley are head to head; one of them does not increase upon the other.
ai.seo_question: What is the rule for exchanging wheat for barley in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi specifies the rule of 'mithl bi-mithl' (equal measure for equal measure) for wheat and barley, ensuring fairness in direct commodity exchange to prevent riba (usury). In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling is foundational for understanding the prohibition of excess in bartering similar foodstuffs, emphasizing that equality in quantity is the primary condition when quality is uniform. The narration highlights the practical application of prophetic economic principles in maintaining social justice and preventing exploitation in daily trade.
